original_title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall might look like Elden Ring, but there's a promising dark fantasy action game here that took me by surprise

en.title: HoYoverse Dares Dark Fantasy With Elden Ring-Like Nodusfall
en.summary: HoYoverse, the studio behind bright anime adventures, has unveiled Nodusfall, a surprisingly dark co-op action game. Early impressions suggest a bold new direction, potentially challenging FromSoftware's established dark fantasy throne.
en.body:
HoYoverse, a company synonymous with vibrant anime aesthetics and beloved titles like **Genshin Impact** and **Honkai: Star Rail**, has thrown a curveball at the gaming world with the official reveal of **Nodusfall**. This new co-op action game, showcased at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, trades in the studio's signature colorful worlds for a grim, dark fantasy setting that has immediately drawn comparisons to **Elden Ring**. The shift is stark: gone are the cheerful companions and fantastical landscapes, replaced by mysterious magics, formidable monsters, and a grittier, more grounded realism that feels distinctly FromSoftware-adjacent. Yet, from initial gameplay glimpses, **Nodusfall** seems poised to carve out its own identity within the genre.

The core of **Nodusfall** revolves around cooperative gameplay, where players, known as Weavers, team up to take on colossal divine beasts. The combat shown emphasizes large weapons, strategic dodge rolls tied to a stamina system, and the necessity of teamwork, with abilities that can even revive fallen allies. This focus on challenging cooperative boss battles, reminiscent of the camaraderie found in games like **Monster Hunter**, sets it apart from HoYoverse's previous offerings. Crucially, the developer has confirmed that **Nodusfall** will be free-to-play and will *not* feature gacha mechanics, a move that could significantly broaden its appeal to players wary of predatory monetization models.

## A Bold Departure for a Beloved Studio

HoYoverse's established success has been built on a foundation of accessible, visually stunning anime-inspired experiences. **Nodusfall** represents a deliberate and ambitious pivot, signaling a willingness to explore more mature themes and gameplay loops. The visual direction, characterized by detailed environments and monstrous enemy designs, aims for a darker, more realistic tone that stands in direct contrast to the bright, cel-shaded worlds of their most popular titles. While the **Elden Ring** comparisons are inevitable given the aesthetic and boss scale, the emphasis on cooperative play offers a distinct flavor. The potential for **Nodusfall** to shake off these comparisons and establish its own unique legacy is palpable, especially with its free-to-play, non-gacha approach.

## Community Anticipation and Expectations

Fans have reacted with a mixture of surprise and excitement. The prospect of a dark fantasy co-op experience from a studio known for its polish and engaging gameplay loops is incredibly enticing. Many are eager to see how HoYoverse translates its knack for compelling world-building and character progression into this new genre. The decision to forgo gacha mechanics has been met with particular approval, seen as a sign of respect for the player base and a commitment to delivering a more traditional action-RPG experience. The community is abuzz with theories about the lore, the types of monsters to expect, and the depth of the cooperative mechanics, all eager for more details on this unexpected venture.

## What's Next

Details regarding **Nodusfall**'s release date and specific platform availability have not yet been announced. Players will be keeping a close eye on HoYoverse's official channels for future updates, gameplay reveals, and beta testing information as the game moves through its development cycle.

content_raw: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get. Gone are the bright colours, cute creatures, and bountiful anime women. In their place, we get all the familiar trappings of dark fantasy: mysterious magics, vicious monsters, and a dingier kind of realism that - and I'm sure we've all thought it - feels a little bit Elden Ring . But from what I played at Gamescom, Nodusfall has the potential to shake off those FromSoftware comparisons and come into its own. Read more
